claim: README/docs: 'Cryptographically prove your installed bytes match the signed witness' (CLAIM-050/051/052/073)
expected: a witness passes only when tampering, missing artifacts and version drift cause a hard failure
observed: On a PRISTINE `npm install ruflo@3.37.0` with no modifications, `ruflo verify` prints its own summary 'pass: 0, drift: 53, regressed: 0, missing: 2' and then prints '[OK] All fixes verified. Installed artifact matches the signed witness manifest.' with a real exit code of 0 (measured directly, not through a pipeline). Mechanism, from the shipped compiled code at dist/src/commands/verify.js:201 — `const allOk = sig.manifestHashOk && sig.publicKeyReproducible && sig.signatureValid && regressedCount === 0;` — excludes driftCount and missingCount from the pass condition by construction. verify.js:244 early-returns on allOk, so the drift warning at :252 is unreachable and 53 SHA-256 mismatches produce no aggregate warning. The --json path shares the semantics (ok: allOk, exitCode 0 at :210). CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER ASSESSMENT IN THIS AUDIT: the signature layer must NOT be credited as sound. verify.js:124 derives the Ed25519 private seed as `createHash('sha256').update(witness.manifest.gitCommit + ':ruflo-witness/v1').digest()`. Both inputs are public — the git commit is in the manifest and the salt is a hardcoded literal in published code — so ANY party can derive the private key and forge a valid signature over any manifest. The `publicKeyReproducible` check at :126 explicitly confirms the key is regenerable from public input and presents that as a security property. The manifest itself is fetched at runtime from DEFAULT_MANIFEST_URL 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruvnet/ruflo/{branch}/verification.md.json' with default branch 'fix/issues-may-1-3' (verify.js:21,139,161) — a MUTABLE feature branch, not a tag or pinned commit. What 'verified' means can therefore change at any time, and requires network access. One missing entry is 'v3/@claude-flow/embeddings/dist/transformers-loader.js', a path that cannot exist in an npm install and whose package another lane independently found is not shipped.
repro: npm install ruflo@3.37.0 in a clean container; run `node node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js verify` WITHOUT piping; echo $?; compare the printed summary with the final verdict line
impact_tailered: The one Ruflo capability Tailered would most want — cryptographic provenance of installed bytes — fails on three independent levels: it makes a false success claim (53 drift, 2 missing, verdict [OK], exit 0); its signature provides no authenticity because the private key is derivable from public data; and its trust anchor is a mutable GitHub feature branch fetched at runtime. Any CI gate invoking `ruflo verify` passes unconditionally. This is the audit's CRITICAL class (reported success with no durable postcondition) and satisfies the 'unverifiable published artifacts' hard blocker.
remediation: Not remediable by a consumer. Upstream must (a) include drift and missing in the pass condition, (b) sign with a real private key held out of band rather than one derived from the public commit hash, and (c) anchor the manifest to an immutable tag or commit. Until then, treat `ruflo verify` as producing no integrity evidence whatsoever.

claim: README/docs: persistent cross-session memory; `[OK] Data stored successfully`
expected: a value reported as stored is readable afterwards, by this process or any other
observed: Coordinator reproduction, independent of lane AUD-L4. Filesystem check by the host, not by Ruflo: the only file created in the repository was `ruvector.db`, and `grep -rl` for the sentinel across the ENTIRE repository tree returned nothing — the value is not on disk in any form. In a SEPARATE brand-new container mounting the same /repo and the same HOME, `ruflo memory retrieve --key coordkey` printed `[WARN] Key not found: coordkey`, after announcing `Using sql.js (WASM SQLite, no build tools required)`. Ruflo cannot read back what it reported storing, and the value never reached disk.
